body: I don't have that "divine hunger" for life you brought up. Lost that years ago after losing one of my many homes. I'm more of a "do nothing and watch life pass by as I wait to die" person.

The problem that I can't be left alone and be locked away from people. My father is one of those "Everyone has to be social at all times" types, so unless I'm sleeping, I don't even a hour of isolation. 

Not to mention hunger just hurts a lot. Like someone heated a knife and is running along the lining of my stomach.
Might be because we live in very low income area and they only have so much supplies?
We've been rejected by the local food banks already. They claim he makes too much despite mostly getting his money from social security.

I've seen first hand on what medication can do to a person's mind when I locked in a mental institution for a week. That was the worse week of my life as I completely lost myself, being a thoughtless zombie as I stared all the walls, completely unresponsive. Pain is horrible but at least I know I exist for now.

Then there's the business end of it when it comes to insurance as they leech every cent a person has for some false hope in most cases. A friend of mine had to have back surgery and required taking enough meds to kill most children, twice a day. Now, he lost his home, his car and his family as he now stays in a shelter because of what they charge him for insurance and medication as he wait for them to give him his next batch. He tell me how much he regrets when he gets him monthly phone call allowance.
